memories.content: The user recorded a family dinner in the calendar for the final week of November.
In a crowded restaurant, the user had to ask several times for orders to be repeated, interrupting the flow of conversation.
When the user held the next gathering at their father's home, they continued the conversation on the sofa after the meal.
At a gathering with loud music prepared by their older sister, the user developed a headache and went outside briefly.
On a day the user held a yard barbecue with their younger brother, the open space dispersed the sound and made conversation easier.
After seeing a message that their maternal aunt would arrive at 5 p.m., the user delayed meal preparation by an hour.
On a day the user waited without knowing their maternal uncle's arrival time, they reheated the food twice.
The user's maternal uncle considers it easier to time his departure when he knows the family meal's start time in advance.
Before scheduling a family meal, confirm the attendees' arrival times and the location with the user.
Available restaurant reservation times may diminish quickly during the year-end gathering season.
The user collects clothes for donation in a large bag beside the entrance.
After emptying an entire drawer at once, the user could not find a charger they needed.
During the next organizing session, the user sorted items by type and put only items to be discarded in the bag.
Even after photographing unworn clothes, the user did not take them out again for one month.
After moving those clothes to the donation bag, the user cleared one closet compartment.
The user nearly discarded an important paper with advertising and checked the recycling box again.
During the next organizing session, the user kept a separate document box and did not mix the papers.
The user's mother asks the user to check whether she needs kitchen items in good condition before discarding them.
Confirm with the user before marking a personal document or another person's property as a disposal candidate.
The local agent cannot determine an object's emotional meaning from frequency of use alone.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: family-meal planning and sensory experience versus household decluttering and disposal safeguards. No claims address the same operational decision closely enough to form a cross-frame relation, and neither side contradicts the other.
